lessons.title: నీళ్ళు, బియ్యం, అన్నం — water and rice
lessons.gloss: water (matching Tamil/Kannada's neer/niiru), and rice raw/cooked — completing the family's water and rice pattern

segments.text: Water closes out 3-against-1 against Malayalam. Rice, though, turns out to have its own twist here.

blocks.title: The word, taken apart - నీళ్ళు — matching the majority

segments.text: నీళ్ళు (nīḷḷu) = "water" — matching Tamil's nīr and Kannada's nīru. Malayalam's veḷḷam is the odd one out among all four Dravidian languages for water, not Telugu.

blocks.title: The word, taken apart - బియ్యం, అన్నం — rice, with a twist

segments.text: బియ్యం (biyyam) = "rice" (raw grain) — Telugu's own word, unlike the shared ari/arisi/akki found in Malayalam, Tamil, and Kannada.
అన్నం (annam) = "cooked rice" (the meal) — matching Kannada's anna closely, both likely Sanskrit-influenced.
So the pattern flips between water and rice: for water, Telugu joins the majority (Tamil/Kannada) against Malayalam; for raw rice, Telugu is itself the odd one out against the other three.

segments.source: [YOU SAY: "biyyam" — raw rice, Telugu's own word]
[YOU SAY: "annam" — cooked rice, matching Kannada's anna]

segments.text: Which language is the odd one out for water, and which for raw rice? (Malayalam is the odd one out for water (veḷḷam); Telugu is the odd one out for raw rice (biyyam, unlike the shared ari/arisi/akki elsewhere).)
